title: A leaf, a flower, a little water
hook: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: the road that runs on love
carry: bhakti: love itself is a road to God
tomorrow: nine ways to love God. which one is yours?

segments.voice: Last week: karma yoga, and its line, seva: serving others changes the one who serves. The birds, the butcher, the curly tail, the half-golden mongoose and the saktu, the barley flour. Today, the second of the three paths.
screen: `SEVA: SERVING OTHERS CHANGES THE ONE WHO SERVES.`

segments.voice: Somebody drives two hours for a birthday. Somebody learns a song on the guitar, badly, for a wedding. Somebody keeps a voicemail for years because of the voice on it. Nobody asked them to. It made no sense on paper. It was love, and love has its own logic. Ask Hindus what their faith is like from the inside, and some won't start with philosophy or with duty. They'll start here: with love, aimed at God. Today, bhakti.
screen: `SOMETHING RIDICULOUS FOR LOVE.` → `IT MADE NO SENSE ON PAPER.` → `LOVE, AIMED AT GOD.`

segments.voice: Bhakti comes from the Sanskrit root bhaj: to share, to take part in, to belong to, and so to love and worship. Bhakti is a sharing. You belong to God, and God, in the bhakti picture, lets you in. The Narada Bhakti Sutra, a short classic of the devotional path, begins by defining it simply: bhakti is supreme love for God. Not an idea about God. Love. In the Gita, Krishna says what that love can look like. Paraphrased: whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water, that offering of love I accept. A leaf costs nothing. By that verse, a single marigold at a roadside shrine counts. The karma path asked: what do you do? The bhakti path asks: who do you love, and how? The Puranas tell of a boy who knew the answer. Prahlada was the son of a demon king, Hiranyakashipu, who hated Vishnu and wanted his son raised to hate him too. One day the king sat the boy on his lap and asked: tell me the best thing your teachers taught you. And the little boy, in his father's lap, gave the wrong answer on purpose. He listed nine ways of loving Vishnu: hearing about him, singing about him, remembering him, and six more, which open tomorrow. The king was furious. Prahlada didn't budge. That's bhakti: love itself is a road to God, open to anyone, even a child in the wrong house. It's why so many Hindu homes begin the day with something small at the shrine: a flower, a lamp, a little water.
screen: `BHAJ — TO SHARE, TO BELONG.` · `SUPREME LOVE FOR GOD.` · `A LEAF, A FLOWER, A FRUIT, WATER.` · `PRAHLADA'S WRONG ANSWER.` · then, large: `LOVE ITSELF IS A ROAD TO GOD.`

segments.voice: Set one small thing down at a home shrine or a windowsill: a flower, a leaf, a little water, a lamp. If you pray, offer it to God as you know God and say one name, Krishna, Rama, Shiva or Devi, once, with love. If you don't, set it down for someone you love, and notice that love wants to give. A leaf is enough.
Bhakti yoga. Devotion as a path: from bhaj, to share and belong. Love for God, offered as simply as a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water.
Your line: bhakti, love itself is a road to God. A leaf is enough. Day two hundred sixty-seven, and the second road begins.

screen: `DAY 267 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: NINE WAYS TO LOVE GOD.`

howItsDone: For many Hindus, bhakti is the heart of daily religious life: offering flowers, water, food or a lamp to a chosen form of God at home or in the temple, singing devotional songs, and repeating a divine name.

trapdoor: what you thought: bhakti is just emotional religion.
what it means: a full path to God through love, as serious as the paths of action and knowledge.

what a scholar hears: the root bhaj means to share or partake; the Gita (esp. ch. 9 and 12) and later the Bhagavata Purana and Narada Bhakti Sutra made devotion a complete path, and bhakti movements reshaped Hindu life across India from the Tamil saints onward.
